description: Build autonomous Python agents with native Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication

summary.one_liner: ProtoLink is a lightweight, A2A-first Python framework for building pluggable, LLM-agnostic agents that communicate through A2A-style cards, tasks, messages, parts and artifacts.
summary.what_it_does: ProtoLink lets you build an Agent from a name and optional pieces: typed Python functions as tools, an LLM from several providers or a mock backend, knowledge for retrieval, MCP tool servers, storage, and transports such as HTTP, SSE JSON-RPC, WebSocket or gRPC. Tools registered from ordinary typed functions can be called directly without a model or network. The agent runs an infer loop in which the model proposes one action at a time (tool call, agent delegation or final answer), with validation and a JSON fallback for smaller local models. Agents can register with a Registry, discover each other and exchange tasks. The framework also offers deterministic Pipeline, Parallel, Router and Graph flows, plus optional features such as local subagents, durable run storage, policy and approvals, cancellation, local tracing, run reports and replay. An optional a2a=True flag serves and calls standard A2A 1.0 JSON-RPC endpoints. A dashboard CLI and a visual Studio builder that generates Python are also described.
use_cases: build a single agent with typed Python tools
run a multi-agent system across processes or machines
connect a local Ollama or llama.cpp model to an agent
let agents delegate tasks to each other over HTTP
answer questions over private documents with citations
wire MCP server tools into an agent
pause an agent for approval and resume it later
trace and replay agent runs for debugging
stack: optional Gemini and other hosted model SDKs
notable: A2A-first design: AgentCard, Task, Message, Part and Artifact are core runtime primitives, with a2a=True translating to canonical A2A 1.0 JSON-RPC
Progressive control: the same constructor accepts names, aliases or fully configured objects, and every module is optional and replaceable
Infer loop with one action at a time, schema validation and a strict JSON action fallback for smaller self-hosted models
Deterministic structured flows (Pipeline, Parallel, Router, Graph) on the same Task-to-Task contract
Dependency-free local tracing, run reports and normalized report diffing for regression testing
caveats: Local command execution runs on the host and is explicitly not a sandbox

Some integrations need extras or API keys: Gemini requires an API key and extra install, Brave web search requires BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY, Google and Microsoft calendar/email adapters need the integrations extra
Remote streaming subscriptions require the peer to advertise streaming support; Ollama streaming requires httpx2
